chunks: From him, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Naḍr al-Armanī, who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام: A group are on a journey, and one of them dies, while among them is a person in janābah, and they have only a small amount of water, enough for only one of the two. Which of them should be given precedence? He said: “The junub performs ghusl, and the dead person is left, because this is an obligation and that is a sunnah.”

So the interpretation concerning these two reports is the same as what we presented regarding the first report. And it has also been narrated: “When the dead person and the junub are together, the dead person is given ghusl and the junub performs tayammum.”

key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel or journey, the state in which this ruling takes place
key_terms.تَيَمَّمَ: performed tayammum, dry ablution in place of water
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: a person in a state of janābah requiring ghusl
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: a prescribed but non-obligatory act in this context
key_terms.فَرِيضَةٌ: an obligatory act in the legal sense
key_terms.مَاءٌ قَلِيلٌ: a small amount of water insufficient for both needs

ai.seo_question: If there is only enough water for either a deceased person’s washing or a junub’s ghusl, which one takes precedence?
ai.summary: This report addresses a legal ruling concerning limited water during travel when there is both a deceased person and someone in janābah. It gives precedence in one narration to the ghusl of the junub because it is a farīḍah, while noting another transmitted report in which the deceased is washed and the junub performs tayammum.
